messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — spike in 503s for inference requests in eu-west-1 starting ~2364805100. Error pattern: routing fallback to legacy model variant causing cascading re-routes and regional capacity thrash. Auto-alert created.

pagerduty: paging @sre-oncall :phone: — urgent

sre-oncall: I'm on it, seeing ~12% 5xx rate on the EU gateway and elevated tail latency. Adding context: most errors align with requests that include `model_variant: auto` in the routing policy.

devon: I just pulled the routing logs — lots of requests hit `variant-legacy` after config push at 2364799000. We shipped schema v2 yesterday which deprecated `default_variant` and introduced `fallback_chain` as an explicit array. Looks like some services still have the old field set; schema migration was supposed to map it, but mapping appears to default to `legacy` instead of preserving previous active variant.

maria: Can you paste the suspect config payloads?

devon: Sure — from a customer-proxy that started failing:

```
route_config: {
  "selector": "*",
  "default_variant": "model-x-legacy",  // deprecated field
  "timeout_ms": 12000
}
```

eng-runtime: The runtime interprets `default_variant`->`fallback_chain` mapping like this today (per the migration script):

```
if default_variant present:
  fallback_chain = [default_variant, global_default]
else:
  fallback_chain = configured_fallback_chain
```

Which is problematic — if `default_variant` existed it forces legacy first and that causes routing to preferentially send to old capacity even when new variants are healthy. That plus a region-level fallback rule causes a loop: EU fails -> fallback to legacy in EU -> legacy saturates -> policy triggers region fallback -> requests bounce between variants/regions.

alex: Paging incident ops: do we have an immediate mitigation? Can we lock routing to a safe variant or temporarily disable fallback behavior?

sre-oncall: Two quick mitigation options:
1) Roll back the schema migration so services see the old behavior (risky, cluster-wide).
2) Patch the routing controller to treat `default_variant` as lower priority (i.e., append, not prepend) or ignore deprecated field if `fallback_chain` is present. We can push a hotfix to the control plane in ~20 min.

support-lead: We already have customers reporting degraded throughput. Early estimate: ~3% of production accounts routed through proxies using the old field (mostly EU-based SaaS customers). We should prepare comms if this is going to be >30min.

maria: Can we quickly flip a config flag to disable cross-region fallback? If requests stay in-region we'll avoid the bounce.

infra-eng: I can flip region_fallback.enabled=false at the control-plane level for EU only. That will take ~5 minutes to roll but should be safe. Doing a gradual change to avoid global blast radius.

eng-runtime: Note: disabling region fallback will reduce failover safety temporarily but will stop the oscillation. Recommend: disable region fallback + patch mapping to preserve existing active variant, then re-enable fallback.

sre-oncall: Doing steps now: 1) infra-eng disables region_fallback for eu-west-1. 2) eng-runtime prepares a hotfix to change mapping behavior. 3) support prepares incident banner. 4) oncall will monitor.

infra-eng: region_fallback.enabled=false applied to eu-west-1 (change-id: cg-2364806001). Rolling config, 3/3 control-plane nodes updated.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Change cg-2364806001 deployed — region fallback disabled for eu-west-1.

sre-oncall: Observability — 5xx rate dropping from 12% -> 4% in last 6 minutes. Latency is normalizing. Good sign.

devon: Hotfix branch ready: alter migration so that when `default_variant` exists and `fallback_chain` is absent we set `fallback_chain = [global_default, default_variant]` (i.e., don't prefer legacy). Also add a validator that rejects configs with both `default_variant` and `fallback_chain` to avoid ambiguity. Pushing now.

eng-runtime: Hotfix rollout in progress (canary -> 10% -> 100%). Canary in eu-west-1 first.

pagerduty: on-call acknowledged by @devon

support-lead: Support triage — initial customer impact: 23 support tickets linked, 2 higher-urgency enterprise customers reporting timeouts. Pulling account IDs and adding to incident timeline.

maria: For postmortem: need to track why migration mapping defaulted to legacy-first. Also how many services used deprecated field — we should inventory via config registry.

devon: Hotfix reached 100% in eu-west-1. No rollback needed so far. Regression tests passed.

sre-oncall: 5xx now ~1%. We're stable. Re-enabling region_fallback will re-introduce risk; recommend keep disabled until we complete inventory and push validator in control plane (ETA 4h).

infra-eng: Affected customers list (IDs): acct-845, acct-412, acct-990, acct-221. We'll send targeted notes via support.

support-lead: Drafting customer message: 

"We experienced degraded inference availability in EU region due to a routing policy mapping issue after a schema migration. We've disabled cross-region fallback and applied a hotfix to preserve variant priority. Impacted customers may have seen timeouts between 12:02–12:20 UTC. We are monitoring and will follow up with remediation steps and a postmortem."

alex: Who will own the postmortem? I can take ownership of the mitigation timeline and SLAs. Maria, can you own the root-cause (schema + migration) and Devon own the remediation (validator + tests)?

maria: Yes. I'll run the config inventory and enumerate services using deprecated fields.

devon: I'll submit the validator PR and a migration audit by EOD. Also adding a schema lint rule to CI so future PRs fail if they add `default_variant` without explicit mapping.

incident-bot: :information_source: Incident status: mitigated (region fallback disabled, hotfix applied). On-call handoff scheduled at 13:00 UTC to @sre-oncall->@alex for follow-up.

sre-oncall: Handoff notes: watch 5xx for next 2 hours, confirm control-plane validator in prod, confirm region_fallback re-enable plan. If we see reversion to >2% 5xx, re-open page.

pagerduty: Handoff alert: @alex will be primary after 13:00 UTC.

support-lead: Sent targeted messages to affected accounts. No major production SLA breaches expected; tracking for compliance.

maria: Adding postmortem checklist items: inventory, migration script review, CI lint, validator PR, communication, re-enable plan with canaries.

alex: Thanks all. Great quick coordination. We'll file the postmortem and schedule a follow-up runbook update to prevent similar surprises.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Thread closed for immediate action. Postmortem assigned.
